review: Reviewed Wren's round-234 request (hand-tie-cord-knot: a learnable bare-hand method to attempt a simple overhand knot in an owned cord, inspect the actual result and conduct a bounded opposing-hand pull trial if its remaining geometry permits; Wren owns the completed 0.30 m two-ply reed cord item-226-wren-2532, whose straight 10 N, 60 s pull at tick 232 establishes no knot feasibility, tail length, flexibility or knotted performance; inputs an exact owned cord, a chosen supported knot and optional bounded force and duration, using the real cord and no tools, anchors, attachments, extra cord or other person; conserve material and paid progress and reject impossible geometry without inventing success; an attempt may succeed, slip, damage the cord or prove infeasible; a trial establishes only its achieved force and duration; no mastery, happiness, reward or improved material) and the World Agent's develop review (learning 3): a general hand-tie-cord-knot(targetId, mode, knot, workId?, trialForce?, trialDuration?) with attempt, inspect, trial, untie and cancel, initially the overhand in a single cord, learnable by anyone; study 3 paid rounds at 0.2 energy; attempt reserves one target and pays three rounds of 0.5 (lay and gently bend a loop, pass the end through, dress and release-check), each recording operation, endpoint positions, tail and knot-path allocation, condition and stage, with a measured geometric or bending failure ending at that stage and charging only work performed; inspection 1 round and 0.2 with no load; untie at most two rounds of 0.5, where a jammed or damaged knot may resist; trial 1 round and 0.5 with force above 0 to 10 N and duration above 0 to 60 s and no implicit trial after tying; cancel free; a versioned cord-knot law representing the overhand crossing sequence and centreline geometry with conserved length, nonpenetration, finite thickness, bend limits, accessible tails and hand spans, and explicit bend, contact, sliding, damage and stress-concentration rules supplied by the developer (unresolved parts to report unavailable); reuse of the hand-twist-fiber-cord material, volume and trial machinery, extended through the knot with independent grips clear of the knot derived from current geometry; the same item, fragments as partitions with provenance, wear exactly once, persistence, pause, resume by workId, cancellation and death rules; versioned events and bounded personal findings; no reward. The specification is self-consistent and every gated physical transition can be given an explicit declared rule, so this is a simplified real mechanism, not a first release. Implemented hand-tie-cord-knot@1 in scope long-ex16: new module packages/world-core/src/long-cord-knot.ts, registered at the end of V7_PACKAGES, with package dependencies foundation-open@1 and hand-twist-fiber-cord@1 (installed at round 221); learning 3 with learningEnergy 0.2, so each study round is paid individually; no prerequisite, cord-making mastery not required; the ability serializes to 3,151 code units within the 3,500 limit; references are empty, so targetId is only the exact id of an own fiber-cord@1 cord or fragment, never a resource name. Every mode refuses arguments of another mode, and every validation (mastery, exact own unreserved target, supported knot, strand law, two-ply section, condition at least 0.5 and the visible minimum length for an attempt, dry footing and clearance, energy, no unfinished own work) precedes any charge or reservation, so refusals spend nothing. Law cord-knot@1 (all values declared modeling assumptions): the cord width is fiber-cord@1's grip width, two ply diameters, and the centreline is its overall length including the 0.02 m loose ends, conserved on the same item as standing tail + knot path + working tail (no new item, quantity, length or attachment; the knot shortens the end-to-end span only). Bend limit: fiber-cord@1's 30 degree two-ply twist already bends each ply at radius one width (helix curvature sin^2 30 / ply radius) and requires engine bend index 0.5; tolerated ply curvature is taken to scale with the material's index, so a lobe of radius R needs 1/width + 1/R within index/(0.5 x width), R >= width x 0.5/(index - 0.5), and an index at or below 0.5 takes no loop; nonpenetration requires R >= width, since a lobe wraps another pass and crossing centrelines lie one width apart; the seated lobe radius is the larger, 2.5 widths for reed (index 0.7); the index itself is never reported, only the tightest loop radius observed. Knot path = 3 pi R + width: an open overhand turns its centreline through at least 3 pi (the 4 pi least turning of a closed knot less the pi of a closing arc) plus one width of transit through the crossings, 10.4 widths at R = width, close to the tightest open overhand. The formation loop radius is the larger of the seated lobe and half of a 0.02 m fingertip opening plus the width; the method centres the knot (standing tail = max(0.02, (centreline - loop knot path)/2)); each hand holds a 0.02 m pinch (fiber-cord@1's free span). Visible pre-cost rejection: the centreline must reach 2 x 0.02 m + the knot path at lobes of one width (or the opening). Round lay-bend-loop: index at or below 0.5 gives 'no-loop'; the end left after one loop turn (2 pi x loop radius) must reach 0.02 m, else 'loop-too-large'; otherwise a held loop with one crossing (state loop, no knot). Round pass-end-through: the end beyond the knot path must reach 0.02 m, else 'end-too-short'; otherwise three crossings (working part over standing part, end under the loop, end out over it), state tucked, a loose undressed knot. Round dress-release-check: the lobes seat to the bend limit and the slack goes evenly into both tails; a tail shorter than the 0.02 m loose end plus one width cannot hold the last crossing on twisted cord, so the end slips out on release and the cord lies straight ('slipped'); otherwise the knot is tied. A measured limit ends the work at that paid stage with the cord released as it actually is; a released untucked loop has no crossing that holds and springs open, while a tucked or tied knot stays. Trial (tied knot only, at least 0.2 unit so a break leaves two lots, each tail at least 0.06 m, a 0.05 m fiber-cord grip kept 0.01 m clear of the knot, else refused with no force applied) reuses fiber-cord@1's machinery: force = min(request, 200 N x health/100, 10,000 N/m x width) with its grip-slip rule; knotted breaking force = fiber-cord@1's 2 x ply area x wet strength x 0.75 x condition divided by the stress concentration 1 + width/(2R) (outer strands of a lobe follow the longer path (R + width/2)/R; 1.2 for reed); elastic extension and creep over the free span between the hands (both tails less the grips plus the knot path); strand damage above half the knotted breaking force; a break at the knot leaves two owned fragments (floor/ceil tenths, half the length each, condition halved, straight knot records marked broke-at-knot with fragment ids); held seconds equal the request only when held; an overhand loaded by both tails cannot spill and a seated knot has no slack, so knot slip is recorded false and load-driven tightening below the seated radius is not represented within the 10 N cap; retained creep lengthens the tails with plies thinned as in fiber-cord@1. Untie: round draw-end-back (state loop), round open-loop (straight, original role restored); the first paid round resists, leaving the knot and stopping the work, when condition is below 0.5 (damaged) or when the passes touch (lobe radius = width) and a recorded trial loaded it to at least half its knotted breaking force (jam, the contact and friction rule); bending set after untying is not represented. While tucked or tied the item's fiber-cord role is 'knotted', so hand-twist-fiber-cord's straight trial, sampling and making refuse it; fiber-cord@1's 0.0005 per round wear no longer reaches that role and this package applies the same rate to it, so wear occurs exactly once; no other ageing, loosening or maintenance is added. Work: the cord itself is reserved through the paid-work escrow (no portion item is created); an unworked round, low energy, standing in water or another person within the body radius plus half the cord pauses before payment (cord-knot-paused); resuming by its mode and workId rechecks the cord and pays only the next stage (cord-knot-resumed); a new attempt on a loose undressed knot pays only the dressing round; cancel (no energy) releases the reservation once and leaves the actual configuration; death leaves the cord ownerless at the death position once; nothing is refunded. Inspect (targetId or own workId; 1 round, 0.2) reports fiber-cord@1's inspection view plus knot state, crossings, lobe and loop sizes, knot path, tails, extent, end-to-end span, centreline and recorded straight and knotted tests as an unverified record, with knotted breaking force and safe load stated as unknown. Events: cord-knot-started, -stage, -infeasible, -paused, -resumed, -tied, -slipped, -resisted, -untied, -cancelled, -stopped, -inspected, -trial, -damaged and -broken, each with actor, item and work ids, law and revision, before and after geometry and condition, requested versus achieved force and time, and fragment ids. Experience: attempt, untie and trial outcomes are verified personal records keyed by operation, resource, cord width in mm (and condition band for trials) and outcome, so the first observation of each, including informative failures, emits information-confirmed and repeats confirm nothing; cord-knot-tied is the practice evidence but carries no qualified flag, so no milestone; no satisfaction, pleasure, comfort, nutrition, goal, permission or reward. Visual: visualComponents is empty because cords are carried stack items with no world object; every event carries reusable 'cord-knot' metadata that embeds fiber-cord@1's view (material color, ply diameter, section, condition, fraying, fragments) and adds only knot path and state (state, tightening, crossings and sequence, loop and lobe radius, knot path and location, tails, extent, end-to-end span, control points), with completedAppearance true only after the recorded crossings and passed release check and a trial indicator only on achieved trial events. Reuse: hand-twist-fiber-cord@1's representation and trial code are called through a new FIBER_CORD export appended to packages/world-core/src/long-fiber-cord.ts (STRANDS, breaking, weakening, wetness, crowded, view, look, conditionOf, part, roleOf, metres, newtons, band and the BEND, SOUND, END, HOLD, SPAN, HAND_PULL, GRIP, ROUND_SECONDS, ONSET, WEAR and EFFICIENCY constants); no existing line of that file changed, so its ability text and behavior stay byte-identical (its 15 tests pass); collective-work.ts (workCreate, workPay, workStop), open-physical.ts openMaterial, open-foundation.ts openRemember and forest-climate.ts forestEvent; the staged escrowed work, pause, resume, cancel and death pattern of hand-break-food@1 and hand-weave-fiber-mat@1. ex14 make-and-test-cordage@1, hand-weave-fiber-mat@1, hand-break-food@1 and long-plant-cultivation.ts are unchanged and continuous.ts changed only by the registration, so ex7-ex16 behavior stays byte-identical. Not represented and reported as such: other knot types, knots joining cords, attachments, anchors or hanging loads, load-driven tightening, bending set, moisture change, loosening over time and repair. Tests (apps/simulator/test/long-ex16-hand-tie-cord-knot.test.ts, 10 cases on cords made with the unchanged hand-twist-fiber-cord@1, the thinnest matching item-226-wren-2532) cover scope and the cord-package dependency, three study rounds at 0.2 energy, the size limit, excluded vocabulary, no satisfaction, three paid rounds tying the same item with conserved centreline, load, material and stack count and a single confirmation, completed appearance only after the release check, measured end-too-short, loop-too-large, slipped and no-loop outcomes charging only performed rounds, cost-free refusals (too short, unsupported or missing knot, resource names, raw stock, irrelevant arguments, missing work, no knot to untie, crowding, energy), a held 10 N 60 s trial with achieved versus requested force and a hand-limited one, refused out-of-range, ungrippable (0.048 m tails) or untied trials, refusal of the straight fiber-cord trial on a knotted cord, strand damage and a break at the knot into two conserved fragments, two-round untying back to a straight cord that the cord package trials again, a damaged knot that resists, pause, resume by workId, cancel of a loop (springs open) and of a loose knot (kept) and dressing-only completion, unverified inspection, single wear and personal-only work, and death. A scratch probe on the actual round-234 checkpoint (not committed, no model call) installed the package and showed Wren's cord taking a 0.0203 m tightest loop, tying with a 0.1994 m knot path and two 0.0703 m tails (end-to-end 0.1893 m), holding a 10 N, 60 s trial with 0.0012 m elastic extension and no damage, and untying back to a straight 0.34 m cord.
